drivingQuestion: What is Beit Hillel's reason for fixing the minimum at five sheep rather than two?
outcomeNote: the unit consists only of the question; Rav Kahana answers it in the following unit (chullin.sugya410).

segments.he: וְכַמָּה הוּא מְרוּבֶּה? בִּשְׁלָמָא לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי – תַּרְתֵּי נָמֵי אִיקְּרוֹ ״צֹאן״, אֶלָּא לְבֵית הִלֵּל – מַאי טַעְמָא?
segments.en: § The mishna states: «And how many is numerous?» Beit Shammai say: It is at least two sheep, and Beit Hillel say: It is at least five sheep. The Gemara objects: «Granted,» according «to» the opinion of «Beit Shammai, two» sheep are «also called tzon,» as in the verse cited by Beit Shammai: “That a man shall rear a young cow and two sheep [tzon]” (Isaiah 7:21). Since the mitzva of the first sheared wool is written with regard to tzon, it is logical that it applies to two sheep. «But what is the reasoning of Beit Hillel,» who hold that the mitzva applies only to five sheep, due to the verse: “And five sheep [tzon] made” (I Samuel 25:18)? Why do they not apply the obligation using the broader criterion of two sheep, as the verse quoted by Beit Shammai clearly indicates that two sheep are also called tzon?
